## Question #1

```{r}
library(xml2)
library(httr)
library(stringr)

website <- xml2::read_html("https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=sars-cov-2")

# Finding the counts
counts <- xml2::xml_find_first(website, ".//div[contains(@class, 'results-amount')]//span[contains(@class, 'value')]")

# Turning it into text
counts <- as.character(counts)

# Extracting the data using regex
totalcount <- stringr::str_extract(counts, "\\d[\\d,.]*")

# Removing any commas/dots so that we can convert to numeric
totalcount <- gsub("[,.]", "",  totalcount)

totalcount <- as.numeric(totalcount)
print(totalcount)
```

There are 278,165 results on PubMed for sars-cov-2.

## Question #2

```{r}
# read in text, each line is a separate character
abstracts <- readLines('~/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt', warn = FALSE)
# combine all text into one character
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = '\n')
# split the text whenever 3 new lines occur in a row (indicating two blank lines)
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = '\n\n\n'))
# replace any remaining "\n" symbols with spaces
abstracts <- gsub("\n", " ", abstracts)
# replace multiple spaces with single space
abstracts <- gsub(" +", " ", abstracts)
abstracts[1:2]
```

There are 5,347 results on Pubmed for sars-cov-2 and including "california" in our search of publications from 2020 to 2021.

## Question #3

```{r}
library(stringr)
institution <- str_extract_all(
  abstracts,"\\b(?:University of California(?:,| at)?\\s+(?:San Francisco|San Diego|Los Angeles|Santa Barbara|Santa Cruz|Davis|Berkeley|Irvine|Riverside|Merced)|University of(?!\\s+California\\b)\\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*(?:\\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*|and|of|the))*|[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*(?:\\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*|and|of|the))*\\s+University(?!\\s+of\\b)|[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*(?:\\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*|and|of|the))*\\s+Institute of\\s+[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*(?:\\s+(?:[A-Z][A-Za-z&'-]*|and|of|the))*)\\b")

institution <- unlist(institution)
table(institution)

```

```{r}

institution_counts <- sort(
  table(institution),
  decreasing = TRUE
)


top10 <- head(institution_counts, 10)


top10_institutions <- data.frame(
  Institution = names(top10),
  Frequency = as.integer(top10),
  row.names = NULL
)

print(top10_institutions)
```

The top 10 institutions are listed above. At first, I had a different output with the top institution having almost "4000" search results but it only had "University of California." After changing the Regex, I received a different result now with the full name. However, I noticed that there is two different University of California San Francisco names (one with a comma and one without). I would change the regex to group them together if there is a way to do so.

## Question #4

```{r}
# read in text, each line is a separate character
abstracts <- readLines('~/Downloads/abstract-sars-cov-2-set.txt', warn = FALSE)
# combine all text into one character
abstracts <- paste(abstracts, collapse = '\n')
# split the text whenever 3 new lines occur in a row (indicating two blank lines)
abstracts <- unlist(strsplit(abstracts, split = '\n\n\n'))
```

```{r}
journal <- str_extract(abstracts, "^\\d+\\.\\s+.*?(?=\\.\\s+(?:20|21)\\d{2}\\b)")
head(journal)

titles <- sapply(abstracts, function(x){
  unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[2]
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
head(titles)

authors <- sapply(
  abstracts,
  function(x) {
    unlist(strsplit(x, split = "\n\n"))[3]
  },
  USE.NAMES = FALSE
)
head(authors)

affiliations <- str_extract(abstracts, "(?s)(?<=\\n\\nAuthor information:\\n).*?(?=\\n\\n)")
affiliations <- str_replace_all(
  affiliations,
  "\\s*\\n\\s*",
  " "
)
head(affiliations)
```

```{r}
papers <- data.frame(
  journal, titles, authors, affiliations
)


knitr::kable(papers[1:5, ])
```
